LeashaUser guide - app v0.3.3

    Leasha User Guide

    Find anything on your computer by describing it in plain English: documents, photos, code and years of email, all searched on this machine and nothing sent anywhere.

    For Leasha 0.3.3 · Guide updated 4 October 2026 · Windows 10 and 11

    1Welcome

    Type what you remember about a document, and Leasha gives you the document:

    the safety report Dave sent about Leeds before the audit

    Leasha reads the folders you choose and your Outlook mail, and builds a private index of them on this computer. After that you can find a file by what it says, by what it means, by who sent it, by when, or just by part of its name, and it answers in a fraction of a second.

    Search by meaning

    Words and meaning are searched together, so "the quote for the boiler" finds the email even if it never says "quote".

    Files and mail together

    Documents, PDFs, spreadsheets, photos, code, Outlook archives (.pst), Google Takeout and zip files, in one search box.

    Drives in a drawer

    Catalogue a removable drive once and its files stay findable after you unplug it.

    Stays on this computer

    No account, no cloud and no telemetry. Your documents are only ever read, never changed, moved or deleted.

    One exception, off unless you switch it onThe Chat page can look things up on the web to add to what your own files say. It is off by default. When it is on, only a short search phrase that you can see leaves the computer, never a file name, a passage, an email or your conversation. Searching, indexing and reading stay fully offline either way.

    2Getting started

    Install

    1. Run the installer. In the Leasha folder, double-click run-install.cmd. It checks the scripts first, installs Python and everything Leasha needs, and keeps the window open so you can read what happened. It asks one question: where to build the index. The suggested place, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Leasha, is private to your Windows account.
    2. Check it worked. The installer finishes by running the health check. It must say READY. You can run it again at any time from Settings › Storage & maintenance › Run doctor.
    3. Open Leasha. Use the desktop shortcut, or type .\leasha in the Leasha folder. To run leasha from anywhere, run .\add-to-path.ps1 once. It changes your own PATH only, needs no administrator rights, and -Remove undoes it.
    Why the .\?PowerShell deliberately does not run programs from the folder you are standing in, which protects you from a malicious program dropped there. .\leasha says "this one, here". After add-to-path.ps1 you can leave it off.

    The first time you open it

    A splash screen shows while Leasha starts: "Starting Leasha…", "Opening your index…", "Loading the search engine…" and, on the very first start only, "Downloading the meaning model — one time, about 130 MB". Then the Search page opens with the cursor in the box.

    1. 1What are you looking for? This page appears whenever the box is empty.
    2. 2How much is indexed: "27 documents ready to search." Before the first index run it says "Nothing has been indexed yet. Open the Indexing tab, add a folder, and press Start."
    3. 3The search box. Type a description, or / for filters.
    4. 4Suggestions to try. Each pill types a real search for you, such as "the pdf Dave sent about the boiler" → boiler /from dave /type pdf. Your Recent and Saved searches appear below them once you have some.

    Choose what to index, then index it

    1. Open Settings › What's indexed. Under Folders to index, press Add all four to add Documents, Desktop, Downloads and Pictures, or Add folder… to choose your own. "You can remove any of them afterwards, and nothing is indexed until you press Index."
    2. Open Indexing (the pill at the bottom of the left-hand rail, or Ctrl+I) and press Start indexing, or press F5 anywhere.
    3. Search while it runs. Words become searchable first and meaning catches up behind them, so you do not have to wait for the run to finish.
    ShortcutDrag a folder from Explorer onto the Leasha window. It opens Indexing and indexes that folder straight away.
    Your Google dataDownload your Google Takeout and put the zip in an indexed folder. Gmail is indexed as mail, Keep notes as text and photos with their dates, and nothing connects to Google.

    3The window at a glance

    1. 1Menu bar: File, Edit, View, Go and Help (see Menus and shortcuts).
    2. 2The rail: one button per page. Search, Files, Mail, Code, Chat, Offline, Reports. Up and Down move along it; Enter opens a page.
    3. 3The Indexing pill says what the index is doing ("Up to date", "Indexing", "Paused") with a coloured dot. Click it to open the Indexing page.
    4. 4 Settings.
    5. 5The search box. × clears it, and so does Esc.
    6. 6Scope: "Everything", "Mail only", "Documents only", "Code only".
    7. 7 Pinned working set: a panel where you gather documents from several searches.
    8. 8 Timeline: a band marking when results cluster in time.
    9. 9 Thumbnail grid for image-heavy results.
    10. 10 Preview pane (Ctrl+Shift+P).
    11. 11 View: text size, row spacing and how results are grouped.
    12. 12 More: Interpret, Rerank, dragging results out.
    13. 13Notice line: says when a search did a worse job than usual, and why. Here, meaning-based search is off in the demonstration index.
    14. 14Timeline band (shown because 8 is on). Click a period to narrow the search to it.
    15. 15Status line: how many results and how long the search took.
    16. 16A result: name, where it lives, its state and date, and the passage that matched, with your words highlighted.
    17. 17Kind badge: blue for documents, orange MAIL for email, green for code.
    18. 18Preview of the selected result: its full path, size, date and kind.
    19. 19Your words highlighted in the preview. F3 jumps to the next, Shift+F3 to the previous.
    20. 20 Open "Open the file in the application that owns it".
    21. 21 Show in folder "Open the folder this file is in, with the file selected".
    22. 22 Pin in a window "Opens this document in its own window you can keep beside your work."

    4Searching

    Just type

    Describe what you want in your own words. Leasha answers twice as you type: a quick keyword answer the moment you pause, then the full search (words and meaning together) a moment later. Enter runs the full search at once.

    Naming a kind of file in words (added 2 October 2026). "files type pst", "pst files", "files of type docx" and "word files" are read as the /type filter and shown as a chip you can remove - when your index holds that kind of file. With nothing else typed, the list is every file of that kind, newest first. An ordinary word that is also a file extension ("old files", "key files") is left as words.

    • ↑ ↓ in the box move through the results without leaving the box; Enter opens the selected one.
    • Ctrl+Enter with a result selected shows it in its folder.
    • Esc clears the search. If a find bar is open, the first Esc closes it and the second empties the box.
    • Ctrl+K or Ctrl+F brings the cursor back to the box from anywhere.
    Leasha reads your sentence for youIf you type "from maya" and exactly one sender in your mail matches, Leasha turns it into a sender filter and shows it as a chip under the box. A chip read from your words says Read from "…". Remove it to search for those words instead. Nothing you typed is rewritten. A misspelt word that matches nothing is corrected to the nearest word, and the notice line says so.

    Scope

    The four buttons under the box narrow what is searched:

    ButtonWhat it searches
    EverythingAll of it.
    Mail onlyMessages, showing who sent them and when instead of a path.
    Documents onlyFiles on disk that are not in a code repository.
    Code onlyAnything inside a code repository, whatever its type: a README in a repository counts, a .py file in Downloads does not. For "files that look like code" wherever they are, type type:code.

    Filters: type /

    Type / in any search box and a menu of filters opens. Choose one and the menu stays open, offering values from your own index (your real senders, folders and file types). /type pdf and type:pdf mean the same thing. A /word that is not a filter is searched for as typed.

    TypeMeaningExample

    The same list prints in a terminal with leasha commands.

    Interpret: turn a sentence into filters

    Under More, Interpret (Ctrl+Enter) asks a small local model to turn your sentence into filters. "The query it builds goes into the box so you can read and edit it. If the model is unavailable, your words are searched for unchanged." It runs on this computer, and it never runs on its own. Ordinary searching never uses a model to decide what you meant.

    • Rerank (off by default): "Slower but more precise ordering." It is the same setting as Settings › Search.
    • Drag results out (on by default): "Drag a result straight into Explorer, an email or anywhere else that takes a file." Mail rows cannot be dragged.
    • Drawing previews: "Offer to draw a DWG drawing in its own window so you can see which one it is."

    Working with results

    Double-click a result or press Enter to open it. Right-click for more:

    Menu itemWhat it does
    OpenOpens the file in its own application.
    Show in folderOpens Explorer with the file selected.
    PinAdds it to the pinned working set.
    More like this"Find other results with a similar meaning, using the vector already stored for this one."
    Why is this here?"Says, in plain words, what put this result on the page - your words, meaning, how recent it is, whether you have opened it before. Facts only; it never shows a score."
    See everything from this monthOpens your timeline at the month this file is from: photos, files and mail from then.
    Copy pathCopies the full path.
    Why this result?Copies the explanation to the clipboard.
    File is missing - re-index this folderShown only when the file has gone since it was indexed.

    The pinned working set

    Pin documents from several searches and they gather in a panel beside the results. Open them all, Copy the paths (one per line), Remove takes the selected ones out, and Clear the list empties it. No file is touched.

    The preview pane

    Added 4 October 2026. The Preview toggle that sits on the Search bar is now on Files, Mail and Code too, beside each tab's View button, and on Chat beside Fast/Thoughtful. It shows or hides that tab's own preview pane and remembers your choice per tab; the View menu and Ctrl+Shift+P still do the same thing, and the toggle follows them. The pictures of Files, Mail, Code, Chat, Offline, Reports, Indexing › What gets read and Settings › What's indexed were retaken the same day; the rest predate it.

    Reads the selected result beside the list, without opening its application. Text, PDFs, spreadsheets, e-books, pictures and email are drawn in place. Ctrl+F inside it opens a find bar (Enter next, Shift+Enter previous, Esc closes). For an email, the preview shows a header card (sender, recipients, date, attachments as chips) and the conversation it belongs to; "Click a message to read it here." Open in Outlook opens the original.

    Pinned document windows

    Pin in a window opens a document in its own window that stays put while you search for something else. You can have several. Each has Open the real file, Show in folder, Zoom in / Zoom out (or Ctrl+wheel), Fit width, Rotate, Print and Keep on top. For a photo, Describe asks the local picture model what it shows, and ← → walk the other photos in the folder.

    View options

    • Rows: Compact or Normal. Text size for this list only ("System" follows Windows).
    • One row per document: "A long document matching in five places takes five rows without this."
    • Show why each result matched: the match reason on every row.
    • One row per conversation (Mail): replies fold under one message, and the row says how many it stands for.
    • On tables: Columns to show or hide, and Fit columns to contents. Right-clicking a column heading opens the same menu.

    Saved and recent searches

    Edit › Save this search… (Ctrl+D) names the search in the box so you can run it again. Edit › Saved searches… lists them with Search, Rename…, Delete and Close. A saved search also runs from the box with /saved name, and recent and saved searches appear on the empty Search page.

    5 Files: find a file by its name

    The other kind of search: by name rather than by contents. Any part of the name matches, so "voice" finds "Invoice 2024.pdf". Mail is not listed here; use Mail or Search for that. Shortcut: Ctrl+P.

    • Type at least two characters, or a / filter such as /type pdf or /status skipped. Plain English works here too, and a typo is corrected when the list would otherwise be empty.
    • All locations: "Show files from one catalogued source only."
    • Columns: Name, Size, Modified, Type, Status, Folder. Click a heading to sort and drag one to move it.
    • Right-click: Open, Show in folder, Search inside this file, Pin, Copy path, Copy file name.
    • Attachments in your mail are listed by name too.

    6 Mail

    Your mail as a table you can scan, newest first. Shortcut: Ctrl+M.

    • Columns: From, To, Date, Subject, Messages (how many in the conversation), Attach, Size, Status.
    • Plain words narrow the list by what the messages say.
    • Enter or double-click opens the message for reading inside it.
    • Right-click: Search inside this file, See everything from this month, Copy path, Copy subject, Copy sender.
    • View › One row per conversation folds replies together (off by default).
    Outlook archivesLeasha reads a .pst straight from the file where it can, with no Outlook needed and no lock on the file, and otherwise through Outlook. The choice is under Indexing › What gets read › Email.

    7 Code

    One box over every code repository Leasha has found under your folders. Typing searches the indexed files; a git switch reads the repository's history. Shortcut: Ctrl+E.

    • Search history runs a history search now. "Switches that read history - /history, /introduced, /branch - need this, or Enter: git diffs every commit it walks, so they take seconds." While it runs the button becomes Stop, and Esc stops it too.
    • Git view shows the repositories, their branches and recent commits. Selecting a branch lists the files as of that branch.
    • Enter opens a result in your editor at the matching line (choose the editor under Settings › Search › Opening code results). A history row previews as its commit.
    • Right-click adds Copy repository name, Copy full path, Copy path and line, and Ignore this repository for a folder that is not really one. Its files stay searchable, and you can undo it.
    Every git switch
    SwitchWhat it does
    /branch developSearch these branches instead of the checkout
    /all-branchesSearch every local branch head
    /remote-branchesSearch every remote branch head
    /historySearch every commit, not just the current files (the slow one)
    /commit a1b2c3dSearch one commit, or several
    /range v5.0..v6.0Search between two commits or tags
    /tag v5.1Search one tag or release
    /lifetimeEvery branch, every commit, every tag
    /regex Order[A-Z]+Read the search text as a regular expression
    /wordMatch whole words only
    /ignore-caseIgnore capitals
    /class, /interface, /functionFind where a class, interface or function is declared
    /symbol CustomerIdFind a name used as a whole word
    /endpoint /api/ordersFind an API route or endpoint
    /config ConnectionStringFind a configuration key being set
    /exclude-path, /exclude-fileSkip a folder, or files matching a name or pattern
    /author, /committer, /messageOnly commits by this person, or whose message says this
    /since, /untilOnly commits on or after, or on or before, a date
    /merges noneInclude, exclude or show only merge commits
    /introduced, /removedThe commit where this first appeared, or was deleted
    /changed, /lifecycleEvery commit that changed this; created, changed and removed in order
    /file-history src/Order.csWhat happened to a file, including renames
    /added-only, /removed-only, /deleted-filesOnly added lines, only deleted lines, only commits that deleted a file
    /depth 5000How many commits back to look (default 2000)

    8 Chat

    Talk to Leasha. It reads your files first and answers in plain words, and every numbered source in an answer opens the passage it came from.

    • New chat starts a fresh conversation; the old one stays in the list. Rename and Delete act on the chosen one ("Your files are not touched").
    • Type a question. Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a new line, ↑ ↓ walk the sources on the right. Send becomes Stop while it answers; "What has appeared so far stays on screen."
    • Fast / Thoughtful: "Fast answers sooner; Thoughtful takes longer over harder questions."
    • Under an answer: Copy, Regenerate, Try again and, on your last message, Edit.
    • The shelf above the box lists the documents this chat is using. Keep holds one in scope for follow-up questions; Remove takes it out.
    • It can count and find without a model: "How many PDFs did Dave send in 2019?" is answered from the index itself.
    • Preview on the right (added 4 October 2026; the picture above was taken before it): under the Local sources list is the same preview pane Search has. One click on a source, or on a result inside an answer, shows the document there - a message as its card and text, a file as its pages - with Open, Show in folder and Pin in a window under it. Double-click still opens the file in its own program.
    • Asking for a number, a date or an address (added 4 October 2026): "find my passport number" or "show me the landlord's address" is answered with the value, quoted from the document that holds it, not with a list of every file containing those words. "Find the tenancy agreement" still lists the documents.
    Getting a chat modelChat runs a small language model inside Leasha. Open Settings › Models & AI, and press Download beside the chat model. That button is the only thing on the page that goes online, and only when you press it. If you prefer, Chat can use the separate Ollama program instead ("Chat, Interpret and Describe run on").
    The Web switchHidden unless Settings › Models & AI › "Let Chat look things up on the web" is on (it is off by default). Then each conversation has its own Web switch, off until you turn it on. Before each web search Leasha asks Search the web for: "…"? with Allow and Skip.

    9 Offline: drives in a drawer

    "Drives and folders catalogued for offline search - plug one in later and its files are found by name and content even while it is out of reach. Nothing here happens on its own."

    1. Plug the drive in and press Scan a drive…. Choose the drive or folder.
    2. Give it a name you will remember, such as "Projects 2019", and optionally a note ("top shelf, office cupboard"). Leasha never stores the drive letter, because it changes each time the drive is plugged in.
    3. Unplug it whenever you like. Its files still appear in searches with the state Offline, and /on "Projects 2019" narrows a search to it.

    Rescan reads it again while it is plugged in. Delete removes its catalogue from Leasha; "nothing on the drive itself is touched". If you scan a drive that Leasha already knows under another name, it asks Yes — same as … or No — catalogue as new.

    On each line (added 2 October 2026; the picture above was taken before it). The list has two more columns. Hardware ID is the serial number of the disk itself, as Windows reports it, so two drives with similar names can be told apart and matched to the label on the drive. A network share shows its address instead, and a drive Windows gave no serial for says Not available - a Rescan asks again. Rescan holds a button on every line: one press rescans that source, whichever line is selected. It is greyed out while the source is unplugged or something is already running. Right-click a line for Rescan and Copy hardware ID.

    10 Reports and your Life Timeline

    "What Leasha has catalogued, read out as a document rather than searched. Nothing here changes anything on your drives."

    ReportWhat it answers
    Digital Inheritance"A map of every source Leasha knows about - names, locations and what's in each - for someone who isn't you."
    The Space Report"Which files exist in more than one place, how much room the copies take, and what exists nowhere else - so you know what is safe to clear and what is not."
    Browse your timeline"Everything from a month or year - photos, files and mail together, wherever they are kept now - in the order it happened."

    Export… saves a report as a PDF. You choose which sources to include first.

    The Life Timeline

    "A place to wander, not a search." Pick a year, then a month, or type any two dates, and everything from then appears in the order it happened, with photos as thumbnails.

    • Show: Everything except code, Photos, Videos, Documents and other files, Mail, Program code.
    • Group near-identical photos: a burst or two copies of the same file show as one line. Right-click it for "Show all … separately".
    • Year lists every year that has anything in it, with a count. Month buttons Jan to Dec, or Whole year.
    • Or any dates: From and To, then Show. "Leave one empty to have no limit on that side."
    • Other ways in: a result's "See everything from this month", Mail's right-click, and right-clicking the timeline band on the Search page.

    11 Indexing

    Start, watch, pause and resume an index run, and see what was skipped. Progress is counted in files. Open it from the pill on the rail, Ctrl+I or Go › Indexing.

    Status

    1. 1The four parts of this page: Status, What gets read, Schedule, Tuning.
    2. 2The headline, with counts by state underneath ("Indexed 26 · Offline 1").
    3. 3This index: documents, searchable passages, location and size on disk, and when the next run is due.
    4. 4Meaning-based search covers: the share of passages that can be found by meaning. The rest are findable by exact words.
    5. 5The progress bar. While a run is going, a log below it says what the run is doing, file by file.
    6. 6 Start indexing "Read the folders listed in Settings and add what has changed." Safe to stop and safe to repeat; a second run over unchanged files takes seconds.
    7. 7 Pause / Resume holds the run where it is and gives the computer back. Nothing is lost.
    8. 8 Stop "Stops after the current file." Starting again carries on where it left off.
    9. 9 Scan first counts the files so the bar can show a real percentage. It reads no file contents.
    10. 10 Reset index… deletes everything indexed and starts over. "Your documents are never touched."

    During a run you may see Leasha pause by itself, with the reason written beside it: the computer is busy with other programs, on battery, or short of disk space. It carries on by itself when that passes. Your own Pause is different: it waits for you.

    Under the buttons, panels appear when there is something to show:

    • What the run is doing: a timed log of the run. Filter it to "Warnings and errors", or Copy it. A Force skip button beside a file that is taking too long skips just that file.
    • Skipped files ("{n} files skipped — review"), grouped by cause. Retry these is worth pressing when the cause has gone, such as a file that was locked.
    • Timed-out files: Retry with a longer time limit, giving each file a chosen number of times its usual limit for this retry only.
    • Archived folders: Rescan these folders now.

    What gets read

    Every lever that decides what Leasha reads, grouped by place. Each block starts with a plain sentence saying what the current settings do there, and the sentence changes as you move a lever.

    PlaceSettings
    Files on diskIndex every file by name (a row for every file, even ones nothing can read); Re-check archives every (days); Time limit per file; Index cloud-only files (downloads them), off by default because reading a OneDrive placeholder downloads the whole file.
    EmailSkip a mailbox or archive after no progress for; Outlook archives (.pst): "Automatic - direct if possible, else Outlook", "Direct file reading (no Outlook needed)" or "Through Outlook (MAPI)"; Convert a .pst to .eml files…
    Email attachmentsWhat to read from email attachments: "Names only - nothing is opened", "Documents - Office, PDF and text" (the default), "Documents and pictures - slow", "Everything Leasha can read - slowest".
    Zip archivesRead inside .zip archives; Largest archive to read (MB).
    Pictures and scansImages and scans: text and images together, text first, or images only; Pages of a scanned PDF; How white a photo must be to read as a page; Describe photos in the background; Recognise people in photos on this computer.
    Video and audioRead videos on this computer; Write down what is said in recordings; Longest gap between pictures; Most pictures per video; Speech model size. "Changes here take effect the next time Leasha starts."
    CodeWhich files count as code (also on Settings › What's indexed).

    Schedule

    • Run: "Only when I ask" (the default), "Once, shortly after opening", "Every few hours" (with Every so many hours) or "Once a day" (At a time of day).
    • Index files as soon as they are saved (off by default): watches your folders and adds a file a few seconds after it is saved, renamed or deleted, without a full run. Mailboxes and folders marked Archive are left to the ordinary run, and cloud-only files are never downloaded. While it is on, a folder that contains an indexed folder cannot be renamed or moved; switch it off first.

    Tuning

    Most people never need this page. Defaults uses what this computer's specification implies; Auto-tune refines that with what past runs measured; Manual lets you set every control, within the limits the machine allows. Return to automatic puts everything back and keeps your manual values for later.

    • This machine: Re-detect (after adding memory or a graphics driver) and Benchmark now ("the only way to know whether the graphics card is actually faster here").
    • Compute: Run models on (Automatic, Processor, Graphics card), Files read at once, Threads per model call, Chunks per model call, Use the smaller model file.
    • Resources: Memory ceiling, Pause above (processor %), Stop below (GB free), Warn before a run below, Run at low priority, Pause while on battery.
    • Strategy: Make text searchable first, Embed repeated text once, Word index, Read images (during the run, after it, or only when asked), Reading order (newest first or as found), Index in a separate process, Read files in separate processes.
    • Old Office files: how many are read at once and the longest one may take.

    12 Settings

    Five categories down the left. The filter box at the top ("Filter settings (try "memory")") finds a setting in every category at once. Right-click any setting for Reset "…" to its default. Settings marked "Takes effect the next time Leasha starts." need a restart.

    What's indexed

    • Folders to index: Folder, How it is indexed, Cloud content, Read first. Each folder is Live - re-check every run or Archive - it does not change (walked once, then checked with a single look). Add folder…, Remove, Index this folder first, Rescan archived folders now.
    • Index now, on each folder's line (added 2 October 2026; the picture above was taken before it): a fifth column, Index now, holds a button on every line. It indexes that one folder straight away and takes you to the Indexing page to watch it. Nothing else in the list is read, and nothing indexed from the other folders is touched. The folder is read in full even if its line says Archive. Right-click a line for the same action. If a run is already going, Leasha says so and offers to stop it, as Start does.
    • A file as an entry (added 3 October 2026): Add file… adds one file - a mail archive, say - without adding the folder it sits in. It is indexed with the folders, by the same rules a file inside a folder gets, and its line has Live/Archive, "Read first" and Index now like any other. "Index files as they are saved" watches folders only, so a file entry is read by Start, Index now or the next run.
    • Which files count as code: from "Source code only" to "Everything in the repository". "This only changes the Code tab."
    • File types: every extension, what reads it and whether it is on. Select all, Select none, Add file type..., Reset to defaults, Save file types. "Only show what needs attention" lists the types with a problem.

    Search

    • Search: Rerank results (slower, more precise), how many to rerank, and the rerank model.
    • What search may do for you: Fix obvious spelling (correct and say so, suggest only, or never), Try again with fewer words, Offer filters it recognises, Prefer recent documents, Fold older versions together, Say why a result is here, Explain in plain words, Offer what you searched for before, Search from anywhere with a shortcut (default Ctrl+Alt+L), Pre-fill the box from a text selection. A grid shows which of these apply on each page; the Code page leaves spelling, relaxing, recency and folding off.
    • Opening code results: which editor opens a code result at its line, or a command of your own (myeditor --at {line} {path}).
    • Search history: kept on this computer to improve ranking. Clear search history deletes it.

    Models & AI

    • Models on this computer: what is installed and how much room it takes. Download, Use this, Use recommended models, Delete, Remove copies nothing uses, and Update the list from Hugging Face. Downloading is the only thing here that goes online, and only when you press it.
    • Chat: Chat, Interpret and Describe run on "Inside Leasha" (the default, nothing else to install) or "Ollama" (a separate program). The web settings: Let Chat look things up on the web (off), Web search service, Ask before each web search (on), Show the exact web search phrase (on).
    • People and photo descriptions: Name the people in your photos… opens the Photo Tagger.
    • Ollama (optional): its address and model, Refresh list and Test.

    Appearance

    • Minimise to the notification area and Closing the window keeps it running there, so searching is instant when you come back. Quit properly from the tray icon.
    • Appearance: Follow Windows, Always light, Always dark.
    • Animate panels when they open and close (off by default).

    Storage & maintenance

    • Index storage: Move or change index location… (move it, use one already there, or start a new empty one) and Change the meaning model…. Both say what they will do, and what it costs, before anything changes.
    • Recent activity: the latest log lines, with Copy and Open in its own window.
    • Environment: Run doctor, Check that search works, Save a support bundle…, "Record what I do, to help diagnose a problem", "Let leasha:// links open Leasha", Open the logs folder, Clear logs.
    • Restore defaults removes every setting you have changed, so Leasha's own defaults apply.

    13More ways in

    Search from anywhere

    Press Ctrl+Alt+L in any program and a small search box appears over it. Enter opens the highlighted result; with nothing highlighted, it opens the main window with your search. Tab moves between the count chips ("2 files", "1 email") to show one kind only. Esc or clicking away closes it. If you had text selected, the box can start with it.

    Name the people in your photos

    With "Recognise people in photos on this computer" on (it is off by default) and your photos indexed, Leasha groups similar faces into piles. Open Go › People in photos. Click a pile to name it; drag one pile onto another if they are the same person. "Nothing is named until you name it, and names never leave this computer." Then /who Mum finds the photos.

    The tray icon

    When Leasha minimises or closes to the notification area, its icon by the clock offers Show Leasha, Search…, the indexing state and Quit. Click it to bring the window back.

    leasha:// links

    With "Let leasha:// links open Leasha" on, a link such as leasha://search?q=boiler in a note or email runs that search in Leasha.

The same day the result badges - the small DOC, MAIL and CODE labels on each result - were redrawn in the brand's colours so the word on each can be read, and the window's indigo is now exactly the logo's. The Help menu picture was retaken the same day.

    15Privacy and safety, in plain facts

    • Everything Leasha indexes, and everything you search, stays on this computer.
    • Leasha only reads your files. It never changes, moves or deletes one. Reset, Delete and Clear act on Leasha's own index, never on your documents.
    • The index holds copies of text from your files. Treat it as being as sensitive as the most sensitive thing you index.
    • On a computer with separate Windows accounts, each account gets its own private index. On a shared login, anyone using it can find anything Leasha can read; choose the indexed folders accordingly.
    • Leasha goes online only when you press something that says so: downloading a model, updating or checking the list of models, and a Chat web search you have allowed. Indexing and searching never do.

    16When something is not right

    You seeTry
    "Keyword results only - meaning-based search returned nothing"Indexing › Status shows how much of the index meaning-based search covers. If it is low, let the run finish. In a terminal, leasha stats says the same.
    A file you expect is missingType its name on the Files page, or /status skipped. The Status column says why. Indexing › Skipped files groups the causes, with Retry these.
    Indexing paused by itselfThe reason is written beside it (busy, battery, disk space). It carries on by itself.
    Chat says the chat model is not downloadedSettings › Models & AI › Download beside the chat model.
    An Outlook archive is not readIndexing › What gets read › Email: try "Direct file reading (no Outlook needed)". If Outlook has the archive open, close Outlook or detach it.
    A folder cannot be renamed"Index files as soon as they are saved" is on; switch it off under Indexing › Schedule first.
    Anything elseSettings › Storage & maintenance › Run doctor, then Save a support bundle… The bundle is a zip of the logs and settings that says what went wrong.

    17Words used in Leasha

    WordMeans
    IndexLeasha's private copy of what your files say, kept so search is instant. It can always be rebuilt from your files.
    Index runOne pass over your folders, adding what is new or changed.
    Meaning-based searchFinding text that means the same as your words, even with different words.
    PassageA short piece of a document; search finds passages, then shows their document.
    Indexed / PartialFully searchable / searchable by words, meaning still to come.
    Name onlyFindable by name; nothing could read its contents.
    Skipped / FailedCould not be read this time, with the reason recorded.
    Timed outTook longer than its time limit; retry it with a longer one.
    OfflineOn a catalogued drive that is not plugged in.
    Live / Archive folderRe-checked every run / walked once and then checked with a single look.
    ChipA filter shown under the box, with × to remove it.
    InterpretAsking the local model to turn a sentence into filters you can see and edit.
